analysis:
Examined the new add-on hold feature. AddonPeerPolicy authenticates by kernel audit token (LOCAL_PEERTOKEN), a same-euid check, a dynamic SecCodeCheckValidity against a Developer ID requirement pinned to team SLDQ2GJ6TL, matching team and identifier, and the hardened runtime flag. The DEBUG-only dev identity is compiled out of release builds. ProviderLoop+AddonHold binds the claimed add-on name to the verified signer (line 67) and scopes status, renew and release to the owning identifier (ownedHold). The hold closes admission through the existing serving-drain mechanism, cancels in-flight work after 120s, unloads models, persists hold state, and restores the hold on restart. It does not send provider_drain and does not stop the App Attest worker, so I found no change to A-016 authorization or T-053 binding. Coordinator wire changes (CoordinatorClient+Registration, Codec) add busy fields to register and heartbeat. Busy is sent only beside a draining status, which only reduces routing and exposes no new secrets. The ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy change adds an addonHold busy reason and excludes addon-owned drains from the generic draining reason.

No plaintext, key, attestation or billing regressions were identified. Not visible in the supplied evidence: AddonIPCServer (socket path, mode, framing, per-request versus per-connection re-authentication, exec-after-connect handling), the AddonHold lease clamps (leaseSecondsRange) and vmBytes bounds, AddonHoldStore file permissions, the AddonMachineLock semantics, the mailbox request validation, and the CoordinatorClientCodec/ProviderBusy encoding and whether the coordinator honors busy at register. Whether beginServingDrain(owner: .addonHold) can displace other drain owners is also unverified. These need deeper review, so I set needs_deeper_review=true.

findings.detail: This PR adds a local control surface that can close serving admission, cancel in-flight inference after 120s, and unload every model. Callers are code-signature-authenticated sockets (AddonPeerPolicy.authenticate) and the operator mailbox (handleAddonControl). No TB/T entry covers this boundary: socket location and permissions, per-connection versus per-request authentication, lease bounds, or the rule that an expired lease is kept while the machine lock is held (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:322-334, 142-146). The lock appears to be observed through a plain file, so any same-UID process that takes it could keep the provider held indefinitely. The same-UID user is already the operator (ADV-001), so this is an availability and documentation gap rather than a confidentiality regression. Fix: add a TB entry and threat for the add-on hold, recording the peer policy, lease clamps, machine-lock semantics and fail-open on an unreadable hold record (ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift:366-368).
findings.title: New add-on local IPC/mailbox control channel is not covered by the threat model
